chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Ja'far ibn Sama'ah, from Aban, from a man who had affirmed it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
There is no problem if the man were to apply Al-Khalouq for his wife, but he should not sleep overnight having applied Al-Khalouq.

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no problem / it is permissible
key_terms.يَبِيتُ: to spend the night / to sleep
key_terms.يَتَخَلَّقَ: to apply perfume / to scent oneself

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a man to wear perfume to sleep with his wife according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam Jaafar al-Sadiq (AS) permits a man to wear perfume for his wife but advises against sleeping with it on, likely to preserve the fragrance for morning prayers or to avoid overwhelming the household. This ruling reflects the Shia emphasis on marital intimacy and hygiene, balancing personal adornment with practical considerations for daily worship. The prohibition against sleeping with perfume highlights the importance of maintaining a pleasant state for spiritual activities like Fajr prayer.
